questions.q: What is the grammatical term for the verb form "Hkzeo'k" in the line "eSaus Hkzeo'k thou lafpr" from "Nsolsuk ka xhr"?
questions.a: The verb form "Hkzeo'k" is a perfective participle (कर्मण्य क्रिया विशेषण) functioning as an adjective modifying "thou". A wrong answer such as "past tense verb" reveals that the student confuses participial adjectives with finite verbs and cannot distinguish non-finite forms that carry aspectual nuance.

questions.q: Explain in your own words why the poet uses the imperative mood in "vkg! osnuk feyh fonkbZ!" instead of a declarative statement.
questions.a: The imperative mood directly addresses the addressee (the beloved/nation) and creates an urgent, pleading tone that a declarative statement would lack. A wrong answer like "it shows the poet is ordering someone" misses the emotional nuance: the imperative here expresses helpless longing, not authority.

questions.q: In "dkusZfy;k ka xhr", the line "mM+rs [kx ftl vksj eq¡g fd,µle> uhM+ fut I;kjk" uses a relative clause. Identify the relative pronoun and explain its grammatical role in the sentence.
questions.a: The relative pronoun is "ftl" (जिस), which functions as the locative case marker for "vksj" (occasion/time) and introduces the relative clause modifying "vksj". A wrong answer that picks "ftl" but says it is the subject of the clause shows the student cannot analyze case roles in complex sentences.

questions.q: Compare the use of first-person plural ("gekjk", "esjs") in "dkusZfy;k ka xhr" with the first-person singular ("eSa", "esjh") in "Nsolsuk ka xhr". What does this shift in person reveal about the speaker's relationship to the nation in each poem?
questions.a: "Nsolsuk ka xhr" uses singular to convey intimate, personal grief and individual responsibility, while "dkusZfy;k ka xhr" uses plural to evoke collective ownership and shared destiny. A wrong answer that treats both as merely "patriotic" fails to analyze how grammatical person shapes the speaker's stance.

questions.q: Critique the following student claim: "The poet uses difficult Sanskritised words only to show off his vocabulary." Use grammatical evidence from either poem to support your evaluation.
questions.a: The claim is reductive. Words like "lafpr" (perfected), "eèkqdfj;ksa" (sacrifices), and "f{kfrt" (cremation ground) are not merely ornamental; their morphological complexity (tatsama roots) carries cultural weight and historical resonance that simpler tadbhava words would lack. A wrong answer that agrees with the claim shows the student cannot link register choice to thematic depth.

questions.q: Write two original lines in Hindi that imitate the syntactic inversion found in "Jfer LoIu dh eèkqek;k esa / xgu&fofiu dh rjQ&Nk;k esa" (placing the locative phrase before the verb) to describe a personal memory.
questions.a: Example: "बचपन के आँगन की धूल में / खोये हुए सपनों की गंध में / मैंने अपनी माँ की हँसी पाई।" A poor answer that writes standard subject-verb-object order ("मैंने आँगन में माँ की हँसी पाई") shows the student cannot replicate the poetic device of fronting adverbials for emphasis.
